title: Saraburi Temple Day Trip: Phra Phutthabat & Phra Phutthacha 2026
metaDesc: One-day temple itinerary in Saraburi, Thailand — Wat Phra Phutthabat + Wat Phra Phutthacha, with real opening hours, driving directions from Bangkok, parking tips, and where to eat along the way.
keywords: Saraburi temple day trip, Wat Phra Phutthabat, Wat Phra Phutthacha, one day trip from Bangkok, Saraburi itinerary
h1:
Phra Phutthabat & Phra Phutthacha
Saraburi in One Day
intro: Saraburi's two most famous temples sit in different districts, but they're only about 30 km apart — easy to do both in a single day. Drive up Phahon Yothin from Bangkok and you'll be there in under two hours. This itinerary is timed around each temple's actual opening hours so you don't have to backtrack, don't have to rush, and still have a proper sit-down lunch in between.

blocks.html: Wat Phra Phutthabat Ratchaworamahawihan and Wat Phra Phutthacha are the two temples Saraburi locals and merit-makers think of first. The first enshrines a footprint of the Buddha believed to be one of five according to the Theravada Lankan tradition. The second holds the Phra Phutthacha — a shadow-like image of the Buddha on a rock face — along with a right footprint relic and prehistoric rock paintings at the base of the cliff. Completely different draws, but just a 30-minute drive apart, which makes them perfect for a single trip.

Before you plan the day, note two key times: Wat Phra Phutthabat opens around 06:00, while Wat Phra Phutthacha opens at 07:00 and closes earlier, around 17:00. So this itinerary starts at Phra Phutthabat in the morning, then loops back to Phra Phutthacha in the afternoon — it's also closer to Saraburi town and on the way back to Bangkok, so leaving from there in the evening works out perfectly.
This plan is built for people driving from Bangkok. If you're coming by bus or train, the temple order stays the same — just adjust your departure time.

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.title: Leave Bangkok — Visit Wat Phra Phutthabat

items.activity: Depart Bangkok via Phahon Yothin Road (Highway 1) heading to Saraburi
items.note: About 110 km, roughly 1.5–2 hours depending on traffic. Leaving before 08:00 helps you skip the mid-morning slow stretch.

items.activity: Arrive at Wat Phra Phutthabat Ratchaworamahawihan, Khun Khlon, Phra Phutthabat District
items.note: Open approximately 06:00–18:00. Large free parking area. No admission fee.

items.activity: Climb to the mondop pavilion to pay respects at the Buddha's footprint; admire the stucco reliefs and mother-of-pearl inlaid doors
items.note: Shoes must be removed before entering. Dress modestly — covered shoulders and knees. Incense and offerings are sold at stalls near the entrance.

items.activity: Walk around the temple grounds — chedis, pavilions, and the temple museum
items.note: During the annual Phra Phutthabat Festival (roughly February–March) crowds are heavy. Budget extra time for parking.

items.activity: Lunch near Phra Phutthabat District or at a roadside spot on the way back toward town
items.note: Plenty of options along Phahon Yothin — noodle shops, rice-and-curry stalls, and local souvenir shops are easy to spot from the road.

items.activity: Drive toward Saraburi town, heading for Nong Pla Lai sub-district
items.note: From Phra Phutthabat to Phra Phutthacha is about 30 km, roughly 40 minutes. You can take the bypass to avoid the town center.

items.activity: Arrive at Wat Phra Phutthacha — park, use the restrooms, and get ready to walk
items.note: Open approximately 07:00–17:00. Parking available on site. There are monkeys on the grounds — keep food and loose items secured.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.title: Visit Wat Phra Phutthacha — Hike to the Viewpoint

items.activity: Pay respects at the Phra Phutthacha pavilion at the base of the cliff — look for the faint shadow image on the rock face and the right footprint relic
items.note: This is the temple's main highlight. Give your eyes a moment to adjust and the shadow image on the cliff becomes clearer.

items.activity: Walk over to the prehistoric rock paintings at the base of the hill — line drawings of human figures, animals, and symbols
items.note: Easy to walk past if you're not looking, but there are signs. Take your time scanning the rock walls.

items.activity: Climb the naga staircase — or drive up — to the hilltop viewpoint overlooking Saraburi in the distance
items.note: The stairs are fairly steep. Wear comfortable footwear. If the climb is too much, there's a vehicle road up.

items.activity: Head back down, feed the monkeys if you want, and take a few photos in front of the temple
items.note: Watch your bags, phone, and glasses around the monkeys — they grab quickly.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.title: Coffee Stop — Drive Back to Bangkok

items.activity: Stop at a café or souvenir shop in Saraburi town before heading home
items.note: Saraburi has hillside cafés and local snack shops selling the famous Sao Hai curry puffs — a good pick-up for the road.

items.activity: Get onto Phahon Yothin and drive back to Bangkok
items.note: Leaving before dark means you beat the evening rush hour on the inbound lanes.

blocks.title: Why Visit Phra Phutthabat First
blocks.html: Because Wat Phra Phutthabat is farther from town but opens earlier. Going there in the morning means cooler air and fewer people. Wat Phra Phutthacha is closer to town and sits on the way back to Bangkok — it closes around 17:00, so saving it for the afternoon lines up perfectly. No backtracking, no rushing.

Both temples are doable without your own vehicle, but you'll need to factor in extra connection time. The easiest approach is to take a bus or train to Saraburi first, then arrange local transport from there.

items: Train — Northern and Northeastern line trains stop at Saraburi and Phra Phutthabat stations. From Phra Phutthabat station, take a songthaew (shared pickup truck) or motorcycle taxi to the temple.
Bus (BKS) — Frequent departures from Mo Chit terminal to Saraburi. From the Saraburi town terminal, charter a songthaew or red-plate taxi to both temples. Works especially well if you're in a group.
Charter a local vehicle — Once you're in Saraburi town, hiring a songthaew or local driver to cover both temples in one run is better value than paying per trip. Agree on a price before you get in.
Rent a car from Bangkok — The most flexible option for a one-day plan, since the two temples are in different districts. Driving yourself means you control the clock.

blocks.text: What to Prepare Before You Go

items: Dress modestly — Both are royal temples. Cover shoulders and knees. Shoes come off before entering the pavilion.
Comfortable walking shoes — Wat Phra Phutthacha has a staircase up the hill and some slippery stone sections. Sneakers are a safer call than sandals.
Watch out for monkeys at Phra Phutthacha — Keep bags, food, phones, and glasses secure. Don't tease them.
Bring water and a hat or umbrella — Temple courtyards and the hillside path get direct sun around midday.
Carry cash — Incense, offerings, merit-making donations, and small stalls near the temples are mostly cash only.

blocks.text: Extra Stops If You Have Time

blocks.html: If you get through both temples faster than expected and still have energy, Saraburi has a few easy add-ons that don't pull you too far off route.

items.name: Old Town Market
items.blurb: Walk the market in central Saraburi, try local snacks, and pick up souvenirs. Best visited mid-morning or late afternoon.

items.name: Hillside Café near Muak Lek
items.blurb: If you have spare time and want to unwind, drive a bit further toward Muak Lek for a mountain-view café — though it does take you off the temple route.

items.name: Sao Hai Curry Puffs
items.blurb: The signature souvenir from Saraburi. Pick up a bag from shops in town or roadside stalls on the way back to Bangkok.

faq.q: Can you visit both Wat Phra Phutthabat and Wat Phra Phutthacha in one day?
faq.a: Yes, easily. The two temples are in different districts but only about 30 km apart — roughly a 40-minute drive. The recommended order is Phra Phutthabat in the morning (it's farther away and opens earlier) and Phra Phutthacha in the afternoon (closer to town and on the way back to Bangkok).

faq.q: What are the opening hours for both temples?
faq.a: Wat Phra Phutthabat opens around 06:00 and stays open into the evening. Wat Phra Phutthacha opens around 07:00 and closes at approximately 17:00 — earlier than the first temple. Plan to reach Phra Phutthacha by early-to-mid afternoon at the latest, since you'll still want time to hike up to the viewpoint.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive from Bangkok?
faq.a: From Bangkok via Phahon Yothin Road (Highway 1) to Saraburi is about 110 km and takes roughly 1.5–2 hours. Leaving before 08:00 helps you avoid the mid-morning traffic and arrive at Wat Phra Phutthabat around 09:00.

faq.q: Can I do this trip without a car?
faq.a: You can, but it takes more planning. Take a BKS bus from Mo Chit or a train from Bangkok to Saraburi or Phra Phutthabat station, then arrange local transport. If you're in a group, chartering a songthaew or local driver to cover both temples in one go is more practical and cost-effective than flagging separate rides each time.

Both are royal temples, so dress respectfully — shoulders and knees covered, shoes removed before entering the pavilion. At Wat Phra Phutthacha there's a staircase up the hill, so choose footwear you can actually walk in comfortably.
